items.question: Why are you interested in Cloudflare's Software Engineering Internship? What products or features are you interested in building?
items.problem: Expected "What draws me to Cloudflare is that the network sees real traffic from millions of properties, so the problems are concrete rather than speculative. At Summer Atlantic Capital I built the machine-learning core of an anomaly-detection and alert-prioritization system, including the event-ingestion pipeline, a versioned FastAPI detection service, temporal sequence models over event streams, and a learning-to-rank layer. The lesson that stuck was that a detector producing too many alerts creates a second problem instead of solving the first, which is why I also built a retrieval-augmented explanation layer so an analyst could see why something fired. That is the kind of work I would want to do at Cloudflare: detection and prioritization on traffic at scale, and the tooling that makes those signals legible to the people acting on them. I am also interested in reliability and safety boundaries in automated systems. In my Playwright-based application agent I put every mutating capability behind fail-closed flags and moved state through an explicit state machine, because automation is only useful if you can predict exactly what it will and will not do. I would like to bring that instinct to systems where a wrong action affects real customer traffic."; page shows "Undergrad"
